newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Catholic monastery rocked by blast in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Catholic monastery rocked by blast in Bosnia.

text.p: Three explosions shattered windows in a Roman Catholic monastery in central Bosnia a week before the scheduled visit of Pope John Paul II to the capital Sarajevo, NATO said on Sunday.

Three explosions were reported at about 11 p.m. (2100 GMT) on Saturday night at a Franciscan monastery in Kraljeva Sutjeska, about 60 km (40 miles) north of Sarajevo, Major Tony White of the NATO-led peace force said.

A guardian at the monastery, Stepan Duvnjak told a Reuters correspondent that two rifle grenades fell in a garden and one hit the main building. "It shattered all the windows. This building has about 40 windows," he said.
No one was injured in the incident, which was the latest in a series of bomb attacks against churches and monasteries in recent months. Two mosques were also targetted.
None of the attacks have caused injuries and no one has claimed responsibility for the bombings which have coincided with political tensions in Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation.
The violence has raised concerns about security surrounding the Pope's historic visit to Sarajevo next Saturday and Sunday.
Bosnian Moslem authorities in the capital say they will deploy thousands of police and place severe restrictions on traffic during the 25-hour visit.
The NATO-led peace force has emphasised that local authorities are primarily responsible for security during the Papal visit.
Pope John Paul II tried to go to Sarajevo during the 1992-95 war but had to cancel the trip because of concern for his security.
